section: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management

accepted.s:
With reference to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They came into force on 1 April 2026.
2. Household hazardous waste has been recognised as a separate ‘special care’ stream.
3. They deal exclusively with industrial hazardous waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026 and recognise household hazardous waste as a separate ‘special care’ stream. They are not confined exclusively to industrial hazardous waste.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that wrongly narrows the scope by using the word ‘exclusively’.

accepted.s: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on:
accepted.x: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on 1 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the date-specific elimination method when several nearby dates are given.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SPSR Nellore — Operation Clean Sweep headquarters
accepted.x: Biomining of legacy waste is associated with Ongole. Anantapur is associated with a proposed 170 TPD waste-processing plant, while CHWTSDFs are located at Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure location-activity pair and eliminate swapped places.

accepted.s: Operation Clean Sweep in Andhra Pradesh during 2026 was conducted:
o: in 113 Urban Local Bodies from 1 April to 31 May
in all villages from 23 May to 20 June
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 20 June to 23 July
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June
accepted.x: Operation Clean Sweep was conducted across all 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June 2026 under the Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra initiative.
accepted.tq: Combine the coverage figure with the correct date range before selecting an option.

accepted.s: A municipal authority requiring an apartment complex to maintain two separate bins for waste segregation is an example associated with:
accepted.x: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) threatened to seal an apartment that did not maintain two segregation bins.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementing local authority from the nature of the municipal enforcement action.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best reflects the reported compliance position of Urban Local Bodies regarding remediation data?
o: More than 75% submit data on time
Less than 10% submit data on time
accepted.x: Only 35% of Urban Local Bodies were reported to submit timely remediation data.
accepted.tq: Watch for percentage-range traps and avoid replacing an exact figure with an approximate extreme.

accepted.s: The campaign associated with SBM-G in 2026 was:
o: Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel - Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath
accepted.x: The 2026 campaign of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was titled “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”. “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu” was the theme associated with June 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the campaign title from the related monthly theme and state initiative.

accepted.s: The theme associated with June 2026 under SBM-G was:
accepted.x: The June 2026 theme was “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu”. It should not be confused with the broader 2026 SBM-G campaign, “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a campaign name and a time-specific theme.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court order of 18 August 2026 regarding responsibility for waste at the threshold held that:
o: Only Urban Local Bodies are responsible for such waste
Only sanitary workers are responsible for such waste
Responsibility begins only after waste reaches a landfill
Generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for such waste
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held that generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for waste at the threshold.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusive responsibility claim by focusing on the phrase ‘not only’.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court’s intervention in solid-waste governance:
1. The relevant order was delivered on 18 August 2026.
2. The Bench included Justice S.V.N. Bhatti.
3. On 1 September 2026, the Court pulled up the Union and State governments for not institutionalising the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The order was dated 18 August 2026, involved a Bench including Justice S.V.N. Bhatti, and the Court criticised the Union and States on 1 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Check each date, institutional actor and judicial action independently before choosing the combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following changes has been reported in the composition of rural waste?
o: A shift from municipal waste towards only industrial hazardous waste
A shift from biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste
A complete disappearance of sanitary waste from rural areas
A shift from plastic waste towards exclusively biodegradable waste
accepted.x: Rural waste is shifting from predominantly biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction of change by comparing the earlier and emerging waste categories.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported compliance position concerning Extended Producer Responsibility for plastic waste?
o: Fewer than 50% of producers comply with EPR targets
EPR targets have been withdrawn for producers
More than 90% of producers comply with EPR targets
Exactly 70% of producers comply with EPR targets
accepted.x: Fewer than 50% of producers were reported to comply with Extended Producer Responsibility targets, leading to criticism about enforceability.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the compliance percentage from the separate figure relating to informal recycling.

accepted.s:
With reference to plastic recycling and waste-pickers, consider the following statements:
1. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers.
2. The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers.
3. About 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers, NAMASTE seeks to formalise them, and approximately 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
accepted.tq: Keep distinct percentages, scheme objectives and population estimates separate while evaluating the statements.

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of ‘invisible e-waste’ commonly discarded with regular waste?
o: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories
Glass bottles, steel cans and paper cartons
Construction aggregates, fly ash and cement bags
Food scraps, garden leaves and crop residue
accepted.x: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories are examples of ‘invisible e-waste’ that may be thrown into regular waste streams.
accepted.tq: Use the category clue and select the cluster of small electronic products.

accepted.s: Weak source segregation in the reported waste-management context is indicated by segregation levels of:
accepted.x: Source segregation was reported to be under 25%, indicating weak segregation practices. This figure is distinct from the 35% of Urban Local Bodies submitting timely remediation data.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related percentages referring to different indicators.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the criticism surrounding the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026?
o: They were criticised on the ground that compliance was eased.
They were criticised for abolishing Extended Producer Responsibility.
They were criticised for completely banning all plastic products.
They were criticised for transferring all plastic regulation to local bodies.
accepted.x: Critics argued that the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026 eased compliance requirements. The criticism did not amount to a complete ban or abolition of EPR.
accepted.tq: Reject extreme interpretations such as ‘completely’, ‘all’ and ‘abolishing’.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 particularly targets:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 targets industrial hazardous waste.
accepted.tq: Match the policy with its stated target instead of selecting an over-narrow category.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the legal frameworks for which the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella?
o: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 as the only framework
accepted.x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella for frameworks including the EIA, Hazardous Waste, Coastal Regulation Zone and Contaminated Sites Rules. It is not described as an umbrella exclusively for the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
accepted.tq: Find the option that improperly uses an exclusive formulation and narrows a broader legal relationship.

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the major institutional concern raised in relation to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: Questions concerning federalism and administrative design
A proposal to eliminate all Urban Local Bodies
A proposal to replace all recycling with incineration
A decision to exempt rural areas from waste regulation
accepted.x: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 have raised questions concerning federalism and administrative design. The other options do not represent the stated criticism.
accepted.tq: Identify the governance dimension of a policy debate rather than an unrelated operational claim.
